primary_cause: Current 2026 evidence reports strengthening dry-bulk freight conditions, including a higher Baltic Dry Index and elevated Capesize rates tied to commodity-vessel demand and tighter vessel supply. Counter-evidence indicates that part of the strength may be rerouting-related and could reverse, but it does not negate the currently observed freight-cycle activation.
counter_evidence: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial and driven by forced rerouting, with a potential 2027 supply glut as the rerouting effect reverses.
